title: Sharp Monocular View Synthesis in Less Than a Second
claim: Our method achieves the best fidelity at near-zero latency, while prior methods trade off quality against orders-of-magnitude more compute time.
layout: 1 panel scatter plot, latency x-axis with broken axis, ours starred
description: A single scatter plot comparing methods on DISTS score (y-axis, lower is better, 0 to 0.4) against latency in seconds (x-axis). The x-axis is broken with slash marks. The left segment runs 0 to 150 s and a short right segment shows about 825 to 850 s. Seven methods appear as labeled colored dots: Flash3D (top left, high error, near-zero latency), LVSM and TMPI (mid-low error, near-zero latency), SVC (about 60 s), ViewCrafter (about 120 s), and Gen3C (far right, about 835 s, low error). SHARP (ours) is a large blue star with a black outline at the bottom-left, with the lowest error and near-zero latency. A legend at top right distinguishes the star (ours) from grey dots (other methods). Light dashed grid lines run behind the points. The eye goes first to the isolated star in the lower-left corner.
caption: Synthesis time on a single GPU versus image fidelity on the ScanNet++ dataset.
abstract: We present SHARP, an approach to photorealistic view synthesis from a single image. Given a single photograph, SHARP regresses the parameters of a 3D Gaussian representation of the depicted scene. This is done in less than a second on a standard GPU via a single feedforward pass through a neural network. The 3D Gaussian representation produced by SHARP can then be rendered in real time, yielding high-resolution photorealistic images for nearby views. The representation is metric, with absolute scale, supporting metric camera movements. Experimental results demonstrate that SHARP delivers robust zero-shot generalization across datasets. It sets a new state of the art on multiple datasets, reducing LPIPS by 25-34% and DISTS by 21-43% versus the best prior model, while lowering the synthesis time by three orders of magnitude. Code and weights are provided at https://github.com/apple/ml-sharp
